stem: Let $X=\{ {=a}, {=a+1}, {=a+2} \}$ and let $f : X \to \mathbb{Z}$ be defined by $f(x)=x+{=k}$. Which of the following writes $f$ as a set of ordered pairs?
solution: Each ordered pair is $(x, f(x))$: the element of $X$ first, its image second.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Writes pairs as (image, element)
proposed_misconceptions.description: Puts f(x) first and x second in the ordered pair.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Lists only the images
proposed_misconceptions.description: Writes the set of images instead of ordered pairs (x, f(x)).

notes: Basic: rule to set of ordered pairs. All four options differ for every a, k.
